unit.title: Check/identify/isolate/rectify malfunctioning electrical machinery appliances and fixtures

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A hotel in Montego Bay reports that a ceiling fan 'runs slowly on every speed'. What should you find out before going to site?
options: The price of a new fan at the nearest hardware store
The fan's model, age and any past repairs
Which guests have complained the most about it
Whether the hotel will pay in cash or by cheque

questions.stem: Where would you find the correct winding resistances and test points for a particular pump motor?
options: On the label of the pump's pressure switch
In any general electrical textbook you can find
From the plumber who first fitted the pump
In the maker's service data for that motor

questions.stem: A fixed water heater is to be checked. After isolating it at its two-pole breaker and local isolator, where should you prove dead?
options: At the heater's terminals, between all conductors
At the breaker only, because it is easier to reach
At a nearby socket outlet on a different circuit
At the shower head, by running some water through

questions.stem: A floor polisher sparks and smells when switched on in a hotel lobby. What should be done with it straight away?
options: Keep using it until the lobby has been finished
Put it back in the store for someone else to look at later
Unplug it, tag it 'Do not use' and take it out of service
Spray the motor with cleaner to stop the sparking

questions.stem: Before electrical tests on an appliance brought in for repair, why do you inspect it carefully by eye?
options: To decide how much to charge before any tests are done
To see whether it is a make that the shop sells
Many faults, such as burnt cords or loose parts, can be seen
So the tests can be skipped if the appliance looks clean

questions.stem: A 220 V water heater element is rated 2 200 W. About what resistance should it read when cold?
A water heater element reads correctly end to end, but the insulation resistance from its terminals to its metal sheath is very low. What will this cause?
options: The water will heat up much more quickly than before
The heater will use less electricity each month
The thermostat will stop switching the element off
Leakage to earth that trips the GFCI (RCD)

questions.stem: A three-phase motor's windings read 5.1 Ω, 5.0 Ω and 2.6 Ω. What does this show?
options: All three windings are healthy and well balanced
One winding has shorted turns
One winding is open circuit and has no path
The motor has been connected in star

questions.stem: A single-phase compressor's terminals read 3 Ω from C to R and 5 Ω from C to S. What should S to R read if the windings are good?
options: 8 Ω
2 Ω
0 Ω

questions.stem: A pressure washer's motor stops after a few minutes of use, then starts again by itself once it has cooled. Which part is acting, and why?
options: Its plug fuse, which blows and then mends itself
Its earth wire, which opens when it gets warm
Its thermal protector, because the motor is overheating
Its on/off switch, which has worn out inside

questions.stem: How should a motor run capacitor be checked once the supply is isolated?
options: Short its terminals with a screwdriver, then look for a spark
Discharge it safely, then measure it with a capacitance meter
Measure the voltage across it while the motor is running
Shake it next to your ear to hear if anything is loose inside

questions.stem: A run capacitor is marked 35 µF ± 5%. It measures 26 µF. What should you do?
options: Keep it in service, as it is close enough to work
Fit a 50 µF capacitor so that the motor runs faster
Add a second 26 µF capacitor in series with it
Replace it with one of the same µF and voltage

questions.stem: A capacitor-start motor starts, but after a few minutes it smells hot and the overload trips. Which fault fits best?
options: The start capacitor has gone open circuit
The supply voltage is too steady and even
The motor's cooling fan is turning too fast
The centrifugal switch stays closed after starting

questions.stem: A pump motor that was flooded in heavy rain gives a low insulation resistance reading. What is usually done, as the maker says?
options: Run it straight away so its own heat dries it out
Dry it out by an approved method, then retest it
Spray the windings with oil to keep the water out
Disconnect its earth so the GFCI stops tripping

questions.stem: A motor runs but makes a rumbling noise that gets louder over the weeks. When isolated, the shaft feels rough when turned by hand. What is the likely fault?
options: The supply voltage is too low for the motor
The start winding has gone open circuit
The bearings are worn
The run capacitor has lost its value

questions.stem: A pump motor runs hotter than normal. Which check is most useful first?
options: Its running current, measured by the authorised person, against the nameplate
Paint the motor a lighter colour so that it takes in less sun
Fit a larger overload so that the motor stops tripping
Take off the fan cover so that more air reaches the motor

questions.stem: A ceiling fan runs slowly on every speed setting, and its bearings are smooth. Which part is most likely faulty?
options: The blade arms, which have been bent out of line
The fan capacitor
The screws holding the ceiling box in place
The plate on the wall switch

questions.stem: An LED panel light flickers and then goes out after a few minutes. The LED board itself is not damaged. Which part usually causes this?
options: The LED driver
The metal ceiling grid that holds the panel
The plastic diffuser cover on the front
The cover plate on the wall switch

questions.stem: An old switch-start fluorescent fitting glows at the tube ends but never lights fully. Which part is the usual cause?
options: The earth wire to the metal body of the fitting
Dust on the diffuser cover of the fitting
The colour of the lamp holders at each end
The starter

questions.stem: How should old fluorescent tubes removed from a hotel be disposed of?
options: Break them into a skip so they take up less space
Burn them along with the other general rubbish
Keep them whole and send them to an approved recycler
Bury them somewhere in the hotel garden

questions.stem: A water heater gives no hot water, and its high-limit cut-out has tripped. Before it is reset, what must you find?
options: Which guest used the most hot water on that day
Whether the reset button is clean and easy to press
Why it tripped, such as a stuck thermostat
How many years ago the heater was installed

questions.stem: One ring on a 220 V electric stove stays at full heat whatever setting is chosen. Which part is most likely faulty?
options: The element of that hob ring on the stove top
The bulb of the oven light
The stove's earth connection
The energy regulator for that ring

questions.stem: A refrigerator's compressor clicks, tries to start and stops every few minutes. Which electrical parts should be checked, dead?
options: The start relay and the overload protector
The door seal and the inside light switch
The defrost drain tube and the drip tray
The temperature dial and the shelf supports

questions.stem: A split air conditioner's fault turns out to be a refrigerant leak. Who should repair it?
options: The electrician, once the supply has been isolated
A certified refrigeration technician
The hotel handyman, using a can of gas from the store
The owner, using a repair kit bought online

questions.stem: An air conditioner's outdoor unit does not start, but the indoor fan runs. With the outdoor unit isolated, which parts are common causes to check?
options: The outdoor contactor and the run capacitor
The air filter inside the indoor unit
The batteries in the remote control
The drain pipe from the indoor unit

questions.stem: A dual run capacitor in an air conditioner has terminals marked C, FAN and HERM. What does HERM connect to?
options: The indoor fan motor above the evaporator
The compressor
The earth terminal on the unit's frame
The room thermostat on the wall

questions.stem: A washing machine will not start a cycle, and its door-lock light never comes on. Which part is most likely faulty?
options: The drain pump at the bottom of the machine
The bearings that support the drum
The door lock (interlock)
The water inlet hose at the back

questions.stem: A house water pump switches on and off every few seconds when one tap is open. Which fault is most likely?
options: The pump motor is too large for the house
The pump's supply cable is too long for it
The pump's earth wire has worked loose
The pressure tank has lost its air charge

questions.stem: A metal-cased Class I appliance is being checked. Which test confirms that its case is properly earthed?
options: An insulation test between line and neutral
A voltage test at the socket outlet it uses
A polarity test at the plug's terminals
Earth continuity from the plug's earth pin to the case

questions.stem: An appliance carries the double-square symbol. What does this tell you?
options: It must always be connected to a 220 V supply
It needs two separate earth wires to be safe
It is double insulated and has no earth connection
It is waterproof and can be used outdoors

questions.stem: A 12-year-old fridge needs a new compressor that costs more than half the price of a new fridge. What is your best advice?
options: Repair it, because a repair is always cheaper
Give both costs, and say replacing may be better value
Tell the owner to keep using it until it stops
Fit a used compressor taken from a scrapped fridge

questions.stem: Why should the faulty parts you replaced be kept and shown to the client?
options: So the client can see what failed and why it was charged
So the same parts can be fitted again later if needed
So the repair shop can sell them on as used spares
So the client can put them out with the household garbage

questions.stem: Which replacement is acceptable for a motor's built-in thermal protector?
options: Any protector that fits into the same space
One with the same rating as the maker's part
A short piece of wire to bridge it out
A larger one so it trips less often in the heat

questions.stem: After a fixed appliance is repaired, which tests are done before the authorised person energises it?
options: Run it for an hour to see whether it gets hot
Check that it looks clean and tidy all over
Ask the client to switch it on and listen to it
Earth continuity, insulation resistance and polarity

questions.stem: During the function test run by the authorised person, which reading is compared with the motor's nameplate?
options: The colour of the casing
The weight of the motor
The running current
The length of its cable

questions.stem: You run a repair bench with three trainees and eight jobs waiting. How should the jobs be put in order?
options: By urgency and safety, agreed with clients
In whatever order the trainees prefer to work
Easiest jobs first so that the numbers look good
Whichever client phones most often goes first

questions.stem: An outdoor security light at a seaside villa keeps failing, and its lamp holder is corroded green. What is the best long-term fix?
options: Clean the holder and refit the same fitting as before
Fit a lamp of a higher wattage in the same fitting
Replace it with a fitting rated for coastal outdoor use
Hose the holder with fresh water to wash off the salt

questions.stem: An outdoor light with a dusk-to-dawn sensor stays on all day. Which part should be checked first?
options: The photocell
The breaker in the panel for that circuit
The lamp fitted in the light
The earth rod outside the building

questions.stem: After a three-phase pump motor is reconnected, the authorised person's short test run shows it turning the wrong way. What is the correct fix?
options: Swap over the earth and the neutral at the motor
Isolate it, then swap any two lines at the motor
Turn the pump body round on its base plate
Run it backwards for a while until it changes over

questions.stem: Why might the authorised person scan a running machine's panel with a thermal imaging camera?
options: To measure the speed of the motor shaft as it turns
To work out the earth fault current
To read the nameplate in a dark room
To find hot joints without touching anything

questions.stem: How should you explain a fault to a guest-house owner who is not technical?
options: In plain words: what failed, why, and the choices
Using as many technical terms as you can, to impress
Only by handing over the bill at the end
By telling the owner that it was their fault

questions.stem: Which job card entry will be most useful for future maintenance of a fan?
options: Fan fixed and working again.
Went to site and did the work on the fan.
Customer is happy with the fan job.
Capacitor 2.5 µF failed; replaced; fan tested

questions.stem: You must check a motor-driven appliance that was running a minute ago. Besides isolating it, what must you allow for?
options: The colour of the paint on its case
Hot surfaces and parts that are still turning
The time of day the appliance is mostly used
The age of the person who usually uses it

questions.stem: Several appliances in one house fail at the same time after a storm. What should you suspect and check first?
options: That they were all bought from the same shop in town
That the owner has been using them all too much
A supply surge or lost neutral
That they were all made for a 110 V supply

questions.stem: What should you leave with the client after repairing a machine?
options: The old parts, left inside the machine's cabinet
A job report with the fault, repair, tests and advice
A note that just says 'Call us if it breaks again'
The test instruments, in case it fails again

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A 110 V kettle element is rated 1 100 W. What resistance should it read when cold, in ohms?
A single-phase compressor reads 2 Ω from C to R and 4 Ω from C to S. What should S to R read, in ohms?
In a single-phase motor, what is the name of the winding that stays in circuit the whole time the motor is running?
A fan capacitor is marked 4 µF ± 5%. What is the lowest reading, in µF, that is still within tolerance?
What is the name of the electronic unit in a light fitting that changes the mains supply to the low-voltage DC that feeds the LEDs?
What is the name of the light sensor that switches an outdoor light on at dusk and off at dawn?
On a light fitting rated IP65, what do the letters IP stand for?
Which instrument shows heat as a picture, so hot connections can be found without touching them?
A motor's nameplate full-load current is 8 A. The authorised person measures 10 A while it runs. By what percentage is it over the nameplate?
A three-phase motor's windings read 4.0 Ω, 4.0 Ω and open circuit. How many windings are faulty?
What is the name of the safety device on a water heater that cuts the supply if the water gets far too hot, and must be reset by hand?
On a dual run capacitor, which part of the air conditioner does the terminal marked HERM connect to?
What words are written on the tag fixed to faulty equipment to stop anyone using it until it is repaired?
Which certified tradesperson must handle the refrigerant gas in a split air conditioner?
What is the name of the part on a single-phase fridge compressor that cuts the power if the compressor gets too hot or draws too much current?

essays.stem: A 220 V pool pump at a hotel in Negril has stopped working. Describe how you would lead the job to check, identify, isolate and rectify the fault.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first ask the hotel staff what happened: whether the breaker or GFCI tripped, whether it made a noise or smell, and when it last worked. I would get the pump's details and the maker's data. On site, I would look for obvious damage, water in the motor or the isolator, and corrosion. Then I would isolate it at the two-pole breaker and the local isolator, lock off, tag and prove dead at the pump terminals between all conductors with a tester checked before and after. With the pump dead, I would check the capacitor after discharging it, measure the winding resistances against the maker's figures, test insulation resistance to earth, and turn the shaft by hand to check the bearings and the pump for a blockage. When the fault is found, I would replace the part like for like, or advise a new pump if the motor is badly damaged. After dead tests, the authorised person runs it and checks the current. I would record the work and explain it to the manager.
markingPoints: Gathers information from staff and the maker's data
Inspects for damage, water and corrosion
Isolates, locks off, tags and proves dead with a checked tester
Checks capacitor, windings, insulation and the mechanical parts in a logical order
Rectifies like for like or advises replacement; tests, function test by the authorised person, records and reports

essays.stem: Explain how a capacitor-start, single-phase motor starts and runs. Then describe the faults that cause (a) humming without starting and (b) starting and then overheating, and how you would test for each with the motor isolated.
essays.modelAnswer: The motor has a run winding and a start winding. At start, the start capacitor is in series with the start winding, which makes a rotating field so the motor can turn by itself. When the motor reaches about three-quarters of its speed, a centrifugal switch opens and cuts out the start winding and capacitor, and the motor runs on the run winding. (a) If it hums but will not start, the start circuit is not working: the start capacitor may be open or weak, the centrifugal switch may be stuck open, or the start winding may be open. A seized bearing can also stop it, so I would turn the shaft by hand. (b) If it starts and then overheats, the centrifugal switch may be stuck closed, so the start winding stays in and burns. With the motor isolated and proved dead, I would discharge and measure the capacitor with a capacitance meter, test the windings for resistance against the maker's values, and check the switch contacts with an ohmmeter at rest and when moved by hand.
markingPoints: Explains run and start windings, the start capacitor and the centrifugal switch
Fault (a): capacitor, switch stuck open, open start winding or seized bearing
Fault (b): centrifugal switch stuck closed, start winding overheating
Discharges and measures the capacitor
Tests windings and switch contacts with the motor isolated and proved dead

essays.stem: A three-phase motor driving a fan in a factory trips its overload. With it isolated, you read winding resistances of 3.2 Ω, 3.2 Ω and 2.1 Ω, and insulation resistance of each winding to earth is good. The shaft turns smoothly. Explain what these readings tell you and what you would recommend.
essays.modelAnswer: A healthy three-phase motor has three windings with nearly equal resistance. Two windings read 3.2 Ω and one reads 2.1 Ω, about a third lower. This shows that the third winding has shorted turns: some of its turns are touching each other, so the winding has fewer working turns. That winding will draw more current and make the motor unbalanced, so it overheats and trips the overload. The good insulation resistance to earth tells me the fault is between turns, not to the frame, and the smooth shaft tells me the bearings and the fan are not the cause. The overload is doing its job and must not be set higher. I would recommend that the motor is rewound by a motor rewinder or replaced with a motor of the same rating, frame and speed, depending on cost and age. I would also check the supply connections and the starter contacts for burning, because a bad connection can cause the same symptom, and record the readings in the motor's history.
markingPoints: Explains that the windings should be balanced
Identifies shorted turns in the low-reading winding
Explains why it overheats and trips, and that the overload must not be raised
Uses the good insulation and smooth shaft to rule out other causes
Recommends rewind or replacement and checks connections, and records the readings

essays.stem: A 220 V, 3 000 W water heater at a guest house trips its GFCI (RCD) whenever it heats. Work out the resistance its element should read, and describe how you would find and fix the fault.
essays.modelAnswer: The element's resistance should be about R = V² ÷ P = 220 × 220 ÷ 3 000 = 48 400 ÷ 3 000 = about 16 Ω. First I would isolate the heater at its two-pole breaker and local isolator, lock off, tag and prove dead at the heater terminals with a tester checked before and after. I would disconnect the element and measure it end to end: about 16 Ω means the heating wire is whole. Then I would test insulation resistance from the element terminals to its metal sheath and to the tank's earth. A low reading means the element's sheath has broken down and current leaks to earth when it heats, which trips the GFCI. I would also check the thermostat, high-limit cut-out and cable for water or damage. The fix is to have the tank drained by the plumber and fit a new element of the same voltage and wattage with a new gasket, then refill before any power is restored. After dead tests, the authorised person energises it, and I record the work.
markingPoints: Calculates about 16 Ω correctly
Isolates, locks off, tags and proves dead with a checked tester
Measures the element end to end and explains the result
Tests insulation resistance to the sheath and earth and explains that a low reading causes the trip
Replaces like for like, drains and refills first, tests, authorised person energises, records

essays.stem: The outdoor unit of a 220 V split air conditioner will not start, though the indoor unit runs. Explain how you would check the electrical side, and where the electrician's work ends.
essays.modelAnswer: I would ask what happened and check that the room thermostat is calling for cooling. Then I would isolate the outdoor unit at its lockable isolator and the breaker, lock off, tag and prove dead at the unit's terminals with a tester checked before and after. I would inspect for burnt wires, insect nests in the contactor, and corrosion from salt air. I would check the contactor's contacts and coil resistance. The run capacitor is discharged safely and measured with a capacitance meter: the HERM section feeds the compressor and the FAN section feeds the outdoor fan, and both must be within the marked tolerance. I would measure the compressor's windings (C–R, C–S, S–R) and test insulation to earth, and check the fan motor. Faulty electrical parts are replaced like for like. If the readings show the compressor is seized or there are signs of a refrigerant problem, such as oil stains, the job is handed to a certified refrigeration technician, because the electrician must not open the refrigerant circuit.
markingPoints: Checks the thermostat call, then isolates, locks off, tags and proves dead
Inspects for burning, insects and corrosion
Checks the contactor and discharges and measures the dual capacitor correctly
Tests compressor windings and insulation, and the fan motor
Hands refrigerant or compressor mechanical faults to a certified refrigeration technician

essays.stem: A hotel on the north coast has many failing light fittings: LED panels flickering, outdoor lights corroded, and old fluorescent fittings not lighting. Explain how you would identify the faults and what you would recommend.
essays.modelAnswer: I would survey the fittings with the maintenance manager and list each fault by room and type. Each circuit is isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead before any fitting is opened. For the LED panels, flicker followed by failure usually points to the driver, especially in hot ceiling spaces, so I would check the driver and its connections and replace it with one matched to the LED board's current and voltage. For the outdoor lights, I would look for water and salt corrosion in the lamp holders and connections, and recommend fittings with a suitable IP rating and corrosion-resistant bodies for coastal use, with sealed cable entries. For old switch-start fluorescent fittings, glowing ends or no light usually point to the starter, tube or ballast; I would suggest replacing them with LED fittings to save energy and maintenance, disposing of tubes through an approved recycler. I would give a written report and a costed plan.
markingPoints: Surveys and records the faults by type and location
Isolates and proves dead before opening fittings
Identifies LED driver faults and matches replacements
Identifies corrosion and recommends suitable outdoor coastal fittings with sealed entries
Addresses fluorescent faults, recommends LED upgrade, safe tube disposal, and gives a report and costs

essays.stem: A small restaurant in Mandeville asks you whether to repair its 10-year-old chest freezer or buy a new one. Explain how you would help the owner decide.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would find out exactly what is wrong by checking the electrical parts with the freezer isolated: the plug and cord, the thermostat, the start relay, the overload protector and the compressor windings. If the fault is the compressor or a refrigerant leak, a certified refrigeration technician would need to quote for that work. I would then compare the full cost of the repair, including parts, labour and GCT at the current rate, with the cost of a new freezer delivered. A common guide is that if the repair costs more than about half the price of a new unit, replacing is often better value, especially for an old unit. I would also consider how much life the old freezer has left, its energy use compared with a newer, more efficient model, the cost of losing stock if it fails again, and the warranty on a new one. I would give the owner the figures in writing, in J$, explain them in plain words, and let them decide.
markingPoints: Diagnoses the fault first, with the freezer isolated; refrigerant work by a certified technician
Compares repair cost (with GCT at the current rate) to replacement
Considers age, remaining life and energy use
Considers risk of stock loss and warranty
Gives written figures in J$ and explains clearly, leaving the choice to the owner

essays.stem: You are in charge of a repair bench with three trainees. Describe how you would organise the bench so that faulty items are handled safely and every repair is checked and recorded.
essays.modelAnswer: Each item is booked in on arrival with a job card: the client, the item, the fault reported and a number, and it is tagged so it cannot be used by mistake. Items wait in a marked area. I would put jobs in order by urgency and safety, and give each trainee jobs suited to their skill, with the maker's data. The bench has an isolated test supply that only I, as the authorised person, or the instructor switch on, and every item is unplugged or isolated before it is opened. Capacitors are discharged and hot parts allowed to cool. Trainees record each test and their findings on the job card. Before any item is reassembled I check the repair, and before it goes back I watch the dead tests (earth continuity, insulation resistance and polarity), then carry out the function test myself. Parts used and time taken are recorded for billing. Finished items get a pass label and a short report; items that cannot be repaired are labelled and the client is told.
markingPoints: Books in each item with a job card and tags it
Prioritises jobs and matches them to trainees' skills
Controls the test supply and requires isolation, discharge and cooling before work
Checks repairs and witnesses dead tests; function test by the authorised person
Records parts, time and results; labels and reports finished or unrepairable items

essays.stem: Late at night, the owner of a guest house calls because the water pump motor is sparking and smoking. Describe what you would tell the owner over the phone, and what you would do when you arrive.
essays.modelAnswer: On the phone I would tell the owner not to touch the pump, to switch off its breaker at the panel if it is safe to reach, and to keep people away. If there is fire, they should call the fire service and use a suitable extinguisher only if it is safe. I would ask them not to switch it back on. When I arrive, I would check that the area is safe, then isolate the pump at the breaker and the local isolator, lock off, tag it 'Do not use', and prove dead at the pump terminals with a tester checked before and after. I would look for the cause: burnt windings, a failed capacitor, water entry or a seized pump. I would tell the owner what I found and arrange a temporary plan for water, such as using a storage tank or a hired pump, until the repair or replacement is done. I would record the event and the isolation, and leave the pump tagged out of service until it is repaired and tested.
markingPoints: Tells the owner to switch off if safe, keep clear and not restart it
Gives fire safety advice
On arrival isolates, locks off, tags and proves dead with a checked tester
Investigates the cause and explains it to the owner
Arranges temporary water, records the event and keeps the pump out of service until repaired

essays.stem: Describe the tests and checks you would carry out after repairing a fixed 220 V machine, before and during its return to service.
essays.modelAnswer: Before any power is restored, I would check the repair visually: correct parts fitted like for like, terminals tight to the maker's torque, cable glands and covers fitted, guards in place, and no tools or off-cuts left. Then I would do the dead tests and record them: continuity of the protective conductor from the supply earth to the machine frame, insulation resistance between live conductors and earth with any electronic parts disconnected, and polarity so the switches and protective devices break the line conductors. When the results are acceptable, the authorised person restores the supply while everyone stands clear. During the function test, the authorised person checks that the machine starts and runs normally, turns the right way, makes no unusual noise or vibration, and that its running current is close to the nameplate. Controls, stops and any GFCI are checked. Finally I would record all results on the job card, explain the work to the user and hand back the machine.
markingPoints: Visual check of parts, torque, glands, covers, guards and tools removed
Protective conductor continuity and insulation resistance (electronics disconnected)
Polarity check
Function test by the authorised person: direction, noise, current against nameplate, controls and GFCI
Records results and hands back to the user

practical1.title: Diagnose and rectify faults on a single-phase pump motor and a three-phase motor, and complete motor test records
practical1.brief: The assessor provides two motors on the training bench, each with planted faults and with the maker's data: a single-phase capacitor-start pump motor (for example a failed start capacitor and a centrifugal switch that sticks) and a three-phase motor (for example one winding with a low reading and a loose terminal link). Neither motor is connected to a supply during the diagnosis; only the instructor runs them, on the protected bench supply, before and after. As a group: (1) the instructor runs each motor briefly so the group can see and hear the symptoms from a safe distance; (2) isolate each motor at its bench isolator, every member fits a personal lock to a hasp, and the leader proves dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after; (3) inspect each motor, then discharge and measure capacitors, measure winding resistances and test insulation resistance to earth, and check the shaft and bearings by hand; (4) compare every reading with the maker's data and decide the fault; (5) rectify what can be rectified on the bench (replace the capacitor like for like, clean and free the switch or fit the spare, remake the link to torque) and write a rewind-or-replace recommendation for the faulty winding; (6) carry out dead tests after repair; (7) the instructor runs each motor and measures its current while the group records it against the nameplate; and (8) complete a motor test record for each. Each member leads the tests on one part and records them. Photograph each stage and hand in both test records.
materials: Single-phase capacitor-start motor and three-phase motor with planted faults, on a protected training bench
Maker's data or nameplate values for each motor
Multimeter with capacitance range or a capacitance meter, and a capacitor discharge tool
Low-resistance ohmmeter and insulation resistance tester
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit, hasp, a lock and tag for each member
Spare start capacitor of the same rating, spare centrifugal switch if available
photos: The group watching the symptoms from a safe distance
The hasp with every member's lock, and proving dead
A capacitor being discharged and measured
Winding resistance and insulation resistance tests
The rectified motors before covers go back on
The instructor's test run, with the current recorded
checklist: Fitted their own lock and followed safe isolation, proving dead with the tester checked before and after
Took and recorded readings correctly, with leads nulled
Compared readings with the maker's data and identified the faults correctly
Rectified faults like for like and remade connections to torque
Carried out dead tests after repair and stood clear during the test run
safety: Only the instructor runs the motors; all trainee work is done dead
Stand behind the marked line during every run
Discharge capacitors with the proper tool before touching terminals
Keep hands, ties and loose clothing away from shafts and couplings

practical2.title: Check and rectify faults on a fixtures bay, then give the client a written report with repair-or-replace advice and a quotation
practical2.brief: The Centre's fixtures bay holds an LED panel with a failed driver, an outdoor light with a photocell and a corroded lamp holder, a switch-start fluorescent fitting with a faulty starter, a ceiling fan with a weak capacitor, and a water heater element assembly with a planted fault (for example a low insulation reading to the sheath). The bay is never connected to a supply during the task. The assessor gives each fault as a client complaint from a guest house. As a group: (1) plan the order of work and who leads each item; (2) isolate the bay at its board, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after; (3) inspect and test each item (continuity, insulation resistance, capacitor value, element resistance worked out from its rating) and identify the fault; (4) rectify the items the assessor allows with like-for-like parts, and tag the others 'Do not use'; (5) carry out dead tests on each repaired item and record them; (6) write a short client report in plain words with each fault, what was done, and a repair-or-replace recommendation for the water heater element and the fluorescent fitting; and (7) prepare a simple quotation in J$ for the recommended work, with GCT shown at the current rate given by the assessor. Each member leads the diagnosis of at least one item and writes part of the report. Photograph each stage and hand in the test records, report and quotation.
materials: Fixtures bay with LED panel, outdoor light and photocell, fluorescent fitting, ceiling fan and water heater element assembly (not connected to any supply)
Client complaint cards and a parts price list from the assessor
Spare LED driver, starter, fan capacitor and lamp holder of the right ratings
Multimeter with capacitance range, insulation resistance tester, low-resistance ohmmeter
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit, lock, hasp and tags, 'Do not use' tags
Test record, client report and quotation forms; a calculator
photos: The work plan with item leaders named
The bay locked off and proved dead
Each fault found, with the test reading
Each repaired item before its cover is refitted
Items that could not be repaired, tagged 'Do not use'
The client report and the quotation
checklist: Isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead correctly
Chose and carried out the right tests for their item
Worked out the expected element resistance from its rating correctly
Identified the fault correctly and rectified it like for like, or tagged it out of service
Recorded dead test results after repair
Wrote clear, plain-language report sections with sound repair-or-replace advice
Prepared an accurate quotation in J$ with GCT at the rate given
safety: The bay is never connected to a supply; only the instructor may energise anything
Handle fluorescent tubes carefully and keep them whole for approved disposal
Wear safety glasses when working on fittings above head height, and use steps safely
